    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — pending executive order on critical minerals, ongoing U.S.-Venezuela investment negotiations
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — U.S. strategic control over Venezuelan oil and minerals, Chinese economic displacement in Latin America, mining sector development uncertainty

Synopsis:
    The Trump administration is pursuing expanded U.S. access to Venezuela's mineral wealth (gold, nickel, copper, coltan, uranium) following its seizure of majority control over Venezuelan oil reserves. Post-Maduro ouster, the U.S. is leveraging a now-cooperative interim Venezuelan government to open its mining sector to Western investment. Treasury has already issued OFAC authorizations for Venezuelan-origin minerals. A critical minerals executive order is being drafted. Significant practical obstacles remain: outdated geological data, illegal armed groups controlling key deposits in the Orinoco Mining Arc, weak infrastructure, and ambiguous reserve estimates. Venezuela has no meaningful rare earth reserves. The strategy is explicitly framed as countering China's regional economic influence.
